item.title: Fast Solvers on Disk Domains
item.description: On a disk, the constant-coefficient Neumann problem separates in polar coordinates: Fourier modes in the angle, and one ordinary differential equation along the radius per mode.

item.title: Fast Solvers on Rectangular Domains
item.description: On a rectangle discretised by a uniform grid (for example the pixel-aligned bilinear meshes of Pixel Images and Finite Element Functions), the Discrete Cosine Transform inverts the constant-coefficient Neumann operator in O(n\log n) operations.

item.title: ModularEIT Wiki
item.description: A wiki on the theory of Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT): the physics and mathematics of the forward and inverse problem, finite element discretisation, adjoint-based gradients, optimisation, and classical and learned regularisation.

item.title: Discrete Cosine Transform
item.description: On a uniform grid, the finite element matrices of Neumann problems are diagonalised by discrete cosine transforms (DCT).

item.title: Choosing the Regularization Parameter
item.description: The parameter \beta in a variational objective balances data fit against prior.

item.title: Spectral Sobolev Norms on Rectangles
item.description: The spectral construction of Discrete Fractional Sobolev Norms needs the eigenvectors of a pair of matrices (K, M).

item.title: Stopping Criteria
item.description: Common rules for terminating a reconstruction: Discrepancy principle: stop when \|\mathcal F(\sigma_k)-y^\delta\|\le\tau\delta (\tau\gtrsim1, \delta the noise level).

item.title: Inverse Crime
item.description: An inverse crime is committed when synthetic data are generated with the same numerical model that is later used for the reconstruction: same mesh, same element type, same discretisation of \sigma, no noise.

item.title: Noise Models for EIT Data
item.description: Simulated EIT data must be corrupted with noise to mimic real measurements and to avoid overly optimistic results (see also Inverse Crime).

item.title: Spectral Image Corruption
item.description: To train a denoiser or deblurrer that should later clean EIT reconstructions, one needs pairs (clean, degraded).
